items.title: Unsubsidised petrol, diesel prices rise 25 sen - MOF
items.summary: KUALA LUMPUR: The retail prices of RON97 petrol, unsubsidised RON95 petrol and unsubsidised diesel will each increase by 25 sen per litre for the period from Sept 10 to 16. MOF said diesel prices in the international market also rose faster than crude oil prices due to constraints on refining capacity and declining inventories. If this situation persists, declining inventories and increasingly tight supplies of refined petroleum products could increase risk premiums on global petrol and diesel prices," MOF said.

items.title: Singapore's DBS sued for US$1bil in 1MDB-linked claim
items.summary: SINGAPORE: Liquidators of four companies linked to global 1Malaysia Development Berhad recovery efforts have sued DBS Bank, seeking an estimated S$1.298 billion (US$1.03 billion) in damages, Southeast Asia's largest lender DBS said on Wednesday. DBS rejected the claim and said it would fight it vigorously, adding that the company has made no provision for the lawsuit. © New Straits Times Press (M) Bhd

items.title: BN must not be complacent after Johor, Negri Sembilan victories
items.summary: Umno vice-president Datuk Seri Johari Abdul Ghani said party members must take seriously the message delivered by Umno president Datuk Seri Ahmad Zahid Hamidi during his briefing and work to convince the people of BN's capabilities. He said Umno and BN must also learn from their past weaknesses and make improvements to ensure the coalition continues to earn the people's trust. We must continue working," he said when met after the Umno presidential briefing at the World Trade Centre Kuala Lumpur here.

items.title: Azeez lawyer disputes claim over lock-up attire, handcuffs
items.summary: Counsel Datuk Amer Hamzah Arshad said police had instructed Azeez to change into the lock-up attire shortly before the remand proceedings. Amer said Azeez was then brought before the Sessions Court (Criminal) 2 for the police's remand application, where a two-day remand order was granted. He said Azeez remained under police custody and control at all material times, adding that the handcuffs placed on him were also put on by police and not the Malaysian Anti-Corruption Commission (MACC).

items.title: King, Queen mourn five killed in Sarawak helicopter crash
items.summary: KUALA LUMPUR: Sultan Ibrahim, the King of Malaysia, and Raja Permaisuri Agong Raja Zarith Sofiah, the Queen of Malaysia, have expressed their condolences to the families of those killed in the helicopter crash in Sarawak yesterday. Their Majesties prayed that the families and next of kin of the victims, which include a pilot and Health Ministry personnel, would be granted strength and fortitude in facing the loss of their loved ones. They also hoped the victims' families would be granted strength, fortitude and patience.

items.title: Former subsidiary CEO remanded four more days over corruption probe
items.summary: A source said the remand order, which runs from tomorrow until Sept 13, was issued by Magistrate Ezrene Zakaria after the Malaysian Anti-Corruption Commission (MACC) made the application at the Putrajaya Magistrate's Court here this morning. "The remand application was made after the suspect's initial remand period ended today. The suspect was previously remanded for three days from last Monday," the source said.

items.title: Umno president urges party to strengthen solidarity, machinery
items.summary: KUALA LUMPUR, Sept 9 — Strengthening solidarity, streamlining party machinery and staying close to the people were among the key messages delivered by Umno president Datuk Seri Dr Ahmad Zahid Hamidi at a briefing today, as the party gears up for the next election. Umno vice-president Datuk Seri Mohamed Khaled Nordin said Ahmad Zahid urged party members to be grateful for the victories in the Johor and Negeri Sembilan state elections, and not to become complacent. Another vice-president, Datuk Seri Johari Abdul Ghani, said Ahmad Zahid reminded party members not to become arrogant following Barisan Nasional’s (BN) victories in the two state elections.

items.title: Malaysia Airlines arranges flights, reimbursements after MH4 diversion
items.summary: KUALA LUMPUR: Malaysia Airlines has arranged additional flights and reimbursements for passengers affected by a UK air traffic control disruption that resulted in flight MH4 being diverted to Manchester. In a travel advisory today, the carrier said it would operate additional flights MH4D (Manchester to London Heathrow) and MH1D (London Heathrow to Kuala Lumpur) to get affected passengers to their final destinations. Stand-up comedian Dr Jason Leong has criticised Malaysia Airlines' crisis management team after Flight MH4 from Kuala Lumpur to London Heathrow was diverted to Manchester Airport, leaving passengers and flight crew without ground support.

items.title: Zahid denies N. Sembilan MB resigned amid royal dispute
items.summary: KUALA LUMPUR, Sept 9 — Umno president Datuk Seri Ahmad Zahid Hamidi has denied claims that Negeri Sembilan Menteri Besar Datuk Ismail Lasim has submitted his resignation amid a dispute involving the state’s royal institution. Ahmad Zahid also denied being present at an alleged meeting where Ismail was purportedly made to sign a proclamation seeking the removal of Negri Sembilan Ruler Tuanku Muhriz Munawir. Ismail himself has denied this,” he said.

items.title: RTD backs MACC action over fake vehicle ownership documents
items.summary: PUTRAJAYA: The Road Transport Department (RTD) has thrown its full support behind the Malaysian Anti-Corruption Commission's (MACC) action over suspected falsification of documents for vehicle ownership transfers. RTD director-general Datuk Aedy Fadly Ramli said the department would give its full cooperation to MACC and leave the matter to the commission. Aedy said RTD remained open to working with MACC to identify any weaknesses or loopholes that could create opportunities for irregularities or abuse of its systems, before implementing appropriate improvements.

items.title: Umno to let top leadership decide GE16 electoral cooperation
items.summary: KUALA LUMPUR: The decision on seat allocations and Umno's partners for the 16th General Election (GE16) will be determined by the party's top leadership. Umno Information chief Datuk Seri Azalina Othman Said said this was among the messages conveyed by Umno president Datuk Seri Dr Ahmad Zahid Hamidi during the presidential briefing held in conjunction with the 2026 Umno general assembly today. "Zahid also mentioned that decisions on party matters must be left to the top party leadership to determine seat allocations and election partners.

items.title: KLK's scion Lee Jia Zhang to take over the mantle starting Oct 1
items.summary: KUALA LUMPUR: Kuala Lumpur Kepong Bhd (KLK) has appointed its chief operating officer Lee Jia Zhang as chief executive officer (CEO), effective Oct 1. Lee, 43, will succeed his father, executive chairman Tan Sri Lee Oi Hian, who served as KLK's CEO for more than three decades. Oi Hian was appointed group chairman and CEO in 1993 and stepped down as the chairman in 2008, but remained CEO until February 2024.

items.title: Zara Qairina inquest: Mother’s assessment unnecessary for psychological autopsy, psychiatrist tells court
items.summary: KOTA KINABALU, Sept 9 — Consultant Forensic Psychiatrist Dr Chua Sze Hung told the Coroner’s Court today that an assessment of the mother of the late Zara Qairina Mahathir was not necessary in the context and framework of a psychological autopsy. Dr Chua, who was recalled to testify, explained that an assessment of the surviving parent was not a proper clinical or methodological substitute for a retrospective assessment of the deceased adolescent’s mental state. Meanwhile, Dr Chua said clinical psychiatric assessment is not meant to be done retrospectively or to answer the manner of death.

items.title: Bursa reprimands Techna-X over delay in annual report, audit adjustments
items.summary: KUALA LUMPUR: Bursa Malaysia Securities Bhd has publicly reprimanded Techna-X Bhd for breaching Main Market listing requirements over the delayed issuance of its annual report and failure to reflect audit adjustments in its quarterly financial results. The regulator said Techna-X failed to issue its annual report for the 18-month financial period ended Dec 31, 2025 by the April 30, 2026 deadline. Bursa Malaysia also found that Techna-X's sixth quarterly report for the period ended Dec 31, 2025, announced on Feb 27, 2026, did not take into account adjustments subsequently identified in the audited financial statements.

items.title: Anwar remembers Capt Zainol Afiq as kind man, pays tribute to pilot’s service (VIDEO)
items.summary: KUALA LUMPUR, Sept 9 — Prime Minister Datuk Seri Anwar Ibrahim remembers Captain Zainol Afiq Bee Sham, the pilot who was killed in yesterday’s helicopter crash in Sarawak, as a kind man of good character. He said the pilot’s service and contributions would always be remembered, and urged his family to inform his staff if they needed any assistance. The prime minister said he would also contact the families of the other victims killed in the crash.

items.title: Finance Ministry: Unsubsidised petrol, diesel prices rise 25 sen per litre from tomorrow
items.summary: KUALA LUMPUR, Sept 9 — The retail prices of RON97 petrol, unsubsidised RON95 petrol and unsubsidised diesel will each increase by 25 sen per litre for the period from September 10 to 16, 2026. MOF said diesel prices in the international market also rose faster than crude oil prices due to constraints on refining capacity and declining inventories. If this situation persists, declining inventories and increasingly tight supplies of refined petroleum products could increase risk premiums on global petrol and diesel prices,” MOF said.

items.title: Former Felda subsidiary CEO gets four-day remand extension in corruption probe
items.summary: A source said the remand order, which runs from tomorrow until September 13, was issued by Magistrate Ezrene Zakaria after the Malaysian Anti-Corruption Commission (MACC) made the application at the Putrajaya Magistrate’s Court here this morning. “The remand application was made after the suspect’s initial remand period ended today. The suspect was previously remanded for three days from last Monday,” the source said.

items.title: EI Power to acquire Shah Alam factory for RM17mil
items.summary: KUALA LUMPUR: EI Power Bhd's unit EI Power Technologies Sdn Bhd is acquiring a freehold factory in Shah Alam for RM17.2 million, mainly funded by proceeds from its initial public offering (IPO). The property sits on 16,100 square feet (sq ft) of freehold industrial land and has a built-up area of about 17,472 sq ft. EI Power said the purchase price was arrived at on a willing-buyer, willing-seller basis, taking into account the property's location and an independent valuation of RM17.3 million by IM Global Property Consultants Sdn Bhd. RM15 million of the consideration will be paid from its IPO proceeds, while the remaining RM2.2 million will come from internal funds, EI Power said in the filing.

items.title: Anwar: PM’s Cup debate nurtures confident, critical young minds
items.summary: KUALA LUMPUR, Sept 9 — The Prime Minister’s Cup Debate Competition is more than a platform for testing debating skills, serving an important role in developing young people who are confident in speaking up, think critically, and respect differing views, Datuk Seri Anwar Ibrahim said. In a Facebook post, the prime minister said the competition continues the legacy of Tun Abdul Razak Hussein by providing young people with a platform to test their courage, deepen their knowledge and sharpen their debating skills. The Prime Minister’s Cup Debate Competition was first held in 1974 at the Malay College Kuala Kangsar in Perak.

items.title: [UPDATED] Zahid denies attending meeting linked to Negri Sembilan royal dispute
items.summary: KUALA LUMPUR: Umno president Datuk Seri Dr Ahmad Zahid Hamidi has denied attending a meeting where Negri Sembilan Menteri Besar Datuk Ismail Lasim signed a proclamation to remove Tuanku Muhriz Tuanku Munawir as the state ruler. Zahid said Umno respected the royal institution, the institution of the Undang and Negri Sembilan's customs. Earlier, Umno information chief Datuk Seri Azalina Othman Said and secretary-general Datuk Dr Asyraf Wajdi Dusuki also denied attending the meeting .

items.title: [UPDATED] Zahid denies receiving resignation letter from Negri Sembilan MB
items.summary: KUALA LUMPUR: Umno president Datuk Seri Dr Ahmad Zahid Hamidi today denied receiving a resignation letter from Negri Sembilan Menteri Besar Datuk Ismail Lasim. The question arose amid the state's royal dispute involving a proclamation to remove Tuanku Muhriz Tuanku Munawir as Negri Sembilan's Yang di-Pertuan Besar. Earlier, Negri Sembilan Umno liaison committee chairman Datuk Seri Jalaluddin Alias said he was unaware of speculation surrounding Ismail's resignation.

items.title: Azalina, Asyraf Wajdi deny attending meeting linked to alleged bid to remove Tuanku Muhriz
items.summary: KUALA LUMPUR, Sept 9 — Two Umno leaders have denied attending a meeting allegedly linked to claims that Negri Sembilan Menteri Besar Datuk Ismail Lasim had signed a declaration seeking to remove Tuanku Muhriz Munawir as the state’s Yang di-Pertuan Besar. The denials came from Umno secretary-general Datuk Asyraf Wajdi Dasuki and Umno information chief Datuk Seri Azalina Othman Said, Harian Metro reported today. Azalina said she was unaware of the alleged matter.

items.title: ENRA in pre-joint bidding cooperation with China Offshore for FSO
items.summary: KUALA LUMPUR: ENRA Group Bhd's indirect subsidiary Hexagon Energy Logistics Sdn Bhd has entered into a pre-joint bidding cooperation agreement with China Offshore Engineering & Technology Co Ltd to jointly bid for a floating storage and offloading (FSO) project in Southeast Asia. In a bourse filing, ENRA said Hexagon and China Offshore intend to work exclusively with each other to prepare and submit a joint bid for the upcoming tender involving the provision of an FSO solution in the region. ENRA said the agreement serves as a non-binding framework and does not create any financial obligations at this stage.

items.title: [UPDATED] 'Who forced him?' Zahid asks over Negri MB's coercion claim
items.summary: KUALA LUMPUR: Umno president Datuk Seri Dr Ahmad Zahid Hamidi has questioned who allegedly forced Negri Sembilan Menteri Besar Datuk Ismail Lasim to sign a proclamation to remove Tuanku Muhriz Tuanku Munawir as the state ruler. he said when asked by reporters here today about Ismail's claim that he had been pressured into signing the proclamation. He said Umno respected the royal institution, the institution of the Undang and the customs of Negri Sembilan.

items.title: LFE secures RM24mil worth of jobs in Ara Damansara
items.summary: KUALA LUMPUR: LFE Corp Bhd has secured three contracts worth a combined RM23.87 million for electrical, mechanical and plumbing works at a commercial development in Ara Damansara, Selangor. Its subsidiary, LFE Engineering Sdn Bhd, accepted the letters of award from Pembinaan Bina Bumi Sdn Bhd to undertake the supply, installation, testing and commissioning works for the redevelopment. The contracts comprise RM13.3 million for electrical and extra-low-voltage services, RM5.3 million for air-conditioning and mechanical ventilation services, and RM5.27 million for cold and hot water and sanitary plumbing services.

items.title: MARKET PULSE PM SEPTEMBER 9, 2026 [WATCH]
items.summary: KUALA LUMPUR: Bursa Malaysia closed flat on Wednesday as escalating tensions in the Middle East pushed Brent crude towards one hundred US dollar a barrel, raising concerns over inflation. The benchmark index closed at 1,714.35. The ringgit strengthened against the US dollar to 4.0590.

items.title: Sirim, NSTP explore consumer awareness on certified products
items.summary: KUALA LUMPUR: Malaysia's Standards and Industrial Research Institute (Sirim) visited Media Prima Berhad at Balai Berita Bangsar here today for an engagement session with New Straits Times Press (NSTP) editors. The visit aimed to explore the use of Media Prima's platforms to raise awareness among consumers about the importance of purchasing Sirim-certified products. [[nid:1529170]] Fauziah added that Sirim was planning to engage with e-commerce sellers to discuss the importance of ensuring products sold online comply with Sirim's certification requirements.

items.title: Ringgit ends easier against US dollar as Middle East conflict weighs on sentiment
items.summary: KUALA LUMPUR: The ringgit ended easier against the US dollar on Wednesday, as market sentiment remained cautious amid an evolving outlook in Middle East, said an economist. Bank Muamalat Malaysia Bhd chief economist Dr Mohd Afzanizam Abdul Rashid said Brent crude prices hit the psychological level of US$100 a barrel today as the conflict between US-Israel and Iran continues, leading to uncertainties over crude oil supplies from the Gulf region. Mohd Afzanizam said consensus estimates are pencilling in headline inflation at 3.4 per cent for August (July: 3.4 per cent), while core CPI is expected to come in at 2.4 per cent, slightly lower than 2.5 per cent in July.

items.title: Alam Maritim Resources CEO Azmi Ahmad to be charged over Tabung Haji probe
items.summary: KUALA LUMPUR, Sept 9 — Alam Maritim Resources Bhd group managing director and chief executive officer (CEO) Datuk Azmi Ahmad will be charged at the Kuala Lumpur Sessions Court tomorrow. Based on a check of the court system, Azmi will be charged at Criminal Sessions Court 14 before Judge Suzana Hussin at 9am. On August 15, Bernama reported that MACC had detained seven individuals comprising a CEO, a company director, a former company director and four former senior management officers of Lembaga Tabung Haji (TH) to assist in investigations into issues raised in the Royal Commission of Inquiry Report on Tabung Haji.

items.title: Kuwait Petroleum offering ship-to-ship transfers outside Hormuz to buyers
items.summary: SINGAPORE: Kuwait Petroleum Corp is offering the option of ship-to-ship transfers outside the Strait of Hormuz to its buyers for safe transportation to final destinations, a company official said on Wednesday. "Whenever it is safe, we are passing some ships through the Strait of Hormuz and we are giving options to do STS (ship-to-ship) operations outside the Strait of Hormuz," Emad A M Al-Kandari, deputy managing director of International Marketing at Kuwait Petroleum Corp, said at the APPEC industry conference. KPC typically offered naphtha on a free-on-board basis before the US-Iran war started.

items.title: Hubline confirms helicopter in fatal Long Lellang crash was operated by subsidiary
items.summary: KUALA LUMPUR, Sept 9 — Shipping and aviation services company Hubline Bhd has confirmed that the helicopter involved in the accident at the Long Lellang Short Take-Off and Landing Airport (STOLport) in Sarawak on Tuesday was operated by its unit, Layang Layang Aerospace Sdn Bhd (LLA). In a filing with Bursa Malaysia today, Hubline said the helicopter, bearing registration number 9M-LLF, was conducting a flying doctor service (FDS) flight when the accident occurred. “The helicopter was operating a FDS flight with five persons on board, including the pilot,” it said.

items.title: Argentina's corn exports set for record as war in Ukraine, European heat wave reshape trade
items.summary: The world's third-largest corn exporter is wrapping up its 2025/26 harvest, estimated at 71.70 million tons, nearly 20 per cent above the previous record set five years ago, according to government data. Normal export volumes for August-September typically reach about 3 million tons, he added. Morocco led the surge, with imports of Argentine corn jumping 133 per cent year-on-year to 1.55 million tons.

items.title: [UPDATED] Man found bound in septic tank at Nibong Tebal house
items.summary: Police had earlier received a missing person's report from the victim's family in the Seberang Prai Tengah district. Penang police chief Datuk Dennis Lim, when contacted, confirmed the incident. A police report lodged at the Sungai Bakap police station on Sept 8 also detailed earlier suspicious transactions involving the victim's account, including transfers to a business account and a personal account.

items.title: Remains of five Long Lellang helicopter crash victims recovered, DNA identification to follow
items.summary: MIRI, Sept 9 — The five victims in the helicopter which crashed in Long Lellang on Tuesday have been recovered, said Sarawak Police Commissioner Datuk Mohamad Zainal Abdullah. Mohamad Zainal said formal identification would be carried out at Miri Hospital, where the remains and tissue samples would also be sent for further examination and DNA testing. Sarawak Police Commissioner Datuk Mohamad Zainal Abdullah said formal identification would be carried out at Miri Hospital, where the remains and tissue samples would also be sent for further examination and DNA testing.

items.title: EM stocks near highs as Asia tech rallies, but Brent's breach of US$100 clouds sentiment
items.summary: The MSCI's EM stocks gauge gained zero point three per cent and was trading near two-month highs. South Korea's tech-laden KOSPI gained, with chipmaker SK Hynix rising three point five per cent, tracking a renewed bout of interest for AI stocks. Regional peer Taiwan also added zero point two per cent.

items.title: [UPDATED] Azalina, Asyraf deny attending meeting linked to Negri Sembilan royal dispute
items.summary: KUALA LUMPUR: Two top Umno leaders have denied attending a meeting linked to the Negri Sembilan royal dispute. The duo, Datuk Seri Azalina Othman Said and Datuk Dr Asyraf Wajdi Dusuki, said they were not present at any such gathering. Azalina replied briefly when asked about the matter, saying: "I don't know.

items.title: Parkson signed 15-year lease for RM111mil in Nanchang, China
items.summary: KUALA LUMPUR: Parkson Holdings Bhd's 54.97 per cent-owned subsidiary, Parkson Retail Group Ltd (PRGL), has renewed the lease for its retail premises in Nanchang, China for 185 million yuan (RM111 million). PRGL, which is listed on the Hong Kong Stock Exchange, said its indirect wholly-owned subsidiary Jiangxi Parkson Retail Co Ltd had entered into a renewal agreement with Jiangxi Kaimei Development Co Ltd on Sept 9. Under International Financial Reporting Standard 16 on leases, the premises will be recognised as a right-of-use asset by the PRGL group.

items.title: Umno delegates enter assembly on an election high after Johor, N. Sembilan wins, with Melaka next on the radar
items.summary: KUALA LUMPUR, Sept 9 — Umno delegates arrived for the first day of the party’s annual assembly today in an upbeat mood following its back-to-back victories in Johor and Negeri Sembilan, with Melaka now emerging as the next electoral target. Umno Youth Damansara committee member Muhammad Najeeh Norazam, 33, said the two state election victories had given delegates a morale boost and changed the atmosphere within the party. Umno Youth Damansara committee member Muhammad Najeeh Norazam, 33, said the two state election victories had given delegates a morale boost and changed the atmosphere within the party.

items.title: Seven years on, Sungai Kim Kim victims win suit against Singaporean directors
items.summary: JOHOR BARU: Seven years after toxic waste was illegally dumped into Sungai Kim Kim, 171 victims won their civil suit against a used tyre processing factory, its two Singaporean directors and a lorry driver. The four defendants were ordered to pay RM100,000 in legal costs to the plaintiffs. However, the plaintiffs failed in their suit against eight other defendants, including the Johor government, then menteri besar the late Datuk Osman Sapian, then state Health and Environment Committee chairman Datuk Sahruddin Jamal, the Johor Environment Department, and the Pasir Gudang Municipal Council, now the Pasir Gudang City Council.

items.title: Trump gave US$45,000 cash gift to 'human printer' aide: US media
items.summary: WASHINGTON: US President Donald Trump gave his executive assistant Natalie Harp a US$45,000 cash gift, US media reported Tuesday. Two other White House employees, Margo Martin and Chamberlain Harris, received similar amounts, according to the Washington Post. The three women described the payments as "Cash Gift for Holidays," the Washington Post reported, citing financial disclosure forms.

items.title: Negri Sembilan Umno urges swift resolution to issue surrounding ruler's position
items.summary: KUALA LUMPUR: Negri Sembilan Umno has called for a speedy resolution to the issue surrounding the position of Yang di-Pertuan Besar Tuanku Muhriz Tuanku Munawir. Its liaison committee chairman Datuk Seri Jalaluddin Alias said he had no knowledge of rumours that Menteri Besar Datuk Ismail Lasim would resign amid the issue. Asked about Ismail signing the Instrument of Proclamation to remove Tuanku Muhriz, Jalaluddin declined to comment further.

items.title: RM1.25b solar hybrid project corruption case: Prosecution challenges ruling allowing Rosmah to adduce additional evidence
items.summary: PUTRAJAYA, Sept 9 — The prosecution has filed an application to stay the Court of Appeal’s decision that granted Datin Seri Rosmah Mansor leave to adduce additional evidence in her appeal against her conviction in the RM1.25 billion solar hybrid project corruption case. The application for stay seeks to temporarily suspend the taking of additional evidence pending the disposal of the prosecution’s appeal before the Federal Court. On August 1, a three-member Court of Appeal bench comprising Justices Datuk Azhahari Kamal Ramli, Datuk Dr Choo Kah Sing, and K. Muniandy allowed Rosmah’s application to adduce additional evidence.

items.title: Long Lellang helicopter crash victims identified through personal belongings - Police [WATCH]
items.summary: KUCHING: The identities of all five victims killed in yesterday's helicopter crash in Long Lellang, Ulu Baram, have been identified through personal belongings found on their bodies. Sarawak Police Commissioner Datuk Mohamud Zainal Abdullah said all five victims were found inside the wreckage of the helicopter, which was registered as 9M-LLF, after it crashed and caught fire at the end of the airstrip. "The victims' remains are scheduled to be flown to Miri Hospital for post-mortem examinations and DNA testing," he said.

items.title: Former Tabung Haji chairman, CEO among five held over hibah, AMLA probes
items.summary: KUALA LUMPUR, Sept 9 — Police have detained five people, including a former Lembaga Tabung Haji (TH) chairman and former chief executive officer (CEO), to assist investigations into matters involving the pilgrimage fund. The five suspects comprise three men and two women aged between 48 and 70, including a former TH chairman, former CEO, former chief financial officer and serving TH personnel. Rusdi said investigations were ongoing.

items.title: Haze: Serian records API 213, highest air pollution level in Sarawak
items.summary: KUALA LUMPUR, Sept 9 — Serian in Sarawak continued to record a very unhealthy Air Pollutant Index (API) reading due to haze this afternoon. Eight other areas in Sarawak recorded unhealthy API readings, namely Samarahan (186), Kuching (183), Sarikei (174), Miri Industrial Training Institute (166), Samalaju (165), Sri Aman (159), Bintulu (157) and Mukah (151). An API reading of zero to 50 indicates good air quality, 51 to 100 (moderate), 101 to 200 (unhealthy), 201 to 300 (very unhealthy) and 300 and above as hazardous.

items.title: Dengue cases soar 66pc, deaths hit 62 in Malaysia, almost double 2025 toll
items.summary: KUALA LUMPUR, Sept 9 — Dengue fever cases nationwide have increased sharply by 66 per cent with 65,979 infections recorded as of Epidemiological Week 35 compared with 39,616 during the same period last year, says Datuk Seri Fahmi Fadzil. The unity government spokesman said the issue was among those discussed at the Cabinet meeting today, with the number of deaths due to dengue also showing a significant increase. He said 62 cases of deaths due to dengue were recorded up to the 35th epidemiological week of this year, compared to 32 cases in the same period last year.

items.title: Umno says Pakatan applying double standard on royal pardons, points to Anwar’s 2018 case
items.summary: KUALA LUMPUR, Sept 9 — Umno today accused Pakatan Harapan (PH) of applying a double standard on royal pardons after the coalition said those convicted in high-profile corruption cases should serve their full sentences. Umno secretary-general Datuk Dr Asyraf Wajdi Dusuki said PH had supported the full pardon granted to Prime Minister Datuk Seri Anwar Ibrahim in 2018 even though he had not completed his five-year prison term at the time. he said in a statement uploaded on Facebook.

items.title: Fahmi: Malaysia ready to help Indonesia fight forest fires, awaiting green light
items.summary: KUALA LUMPUR, Sept 9 — Malaysia is on standby and prepared to assist Indonesia in managing the forest fires that have caused haze in the region, government spokesman Datuk Seri Fahmi Fadzil said today. “For us to deploy our assets to assist, we need the permission by the Indonesian authorities,” said Fahmi, who is also the communications minister. Yesterday, Prime Minister Datuk Seri Anwar Ibrahim called for improvements to the existing Asean mechanism for tackling transboundary haze to ensure such incidents could be addressed effectively.

items.title: MACC: Abdul Azeez chose to remain in purple lock-up attire, handcuffs for court appearance
items.summary: KUALA LUMPUR, Sept 9 — Former Lembaga Tabung Haji (TH) chairman Datuk Seri Abdul Azeez Abdul Rahim chose to wear purple police lock-up attire and handcuffs when he appeared in the Sessions Court here today, the Malaysian Anti-Corruption Commission (MACC) said. In a statement, the MACC said its officers, the police escorting Abdul Azeez and his lawyer had advised him to change into ordinary clothes before he was taken to court. However, the MACC said Abdul Azeez insisted on remaining in the lock-up attire and handcuffs until the charge against him had been read.

items.title: Cabinet expresses condolences to families of five killed in Sarawak FDS helicopter crash
items.summary: KUALA LUMPUR, Sept 9 — The Cabinet today expressed its condolences to the families of the five victims who died in the Flying Doctor Service (FDS) helicopter crash in Long Lellang, Ulu Baram, Sarawak, yesterday. Unity government spokesman Datuk Seri Fahmi Fadzil said Prime Minister Datuk Seri Anwar Ibrahim and all ministers offered their sympathies and condolences at the weekly Cabinet meeting today. Fahmi, who is also the communications minister, said Health Minister Datuk Seri Dr Dzulkefly Ahmad had earlier announced the identities of all five victims.

items.title: Malaysian woman held at Delhi airport with 15kg cannabis worth RM2.2m
items.summary: KUALA LUMPUR, Sept 9 — A Malaysian woman was arrested by Indian authorities after she was caught attempting to smuggle 15 kilogrammes of cannabis, valued at approximately 52.5 million rupees (RM2.2 million), at Indira Gandhi International Airport on Sept 4. Delhi Customs (Airport & General) in a statement on X said the passenger, who arrived from Kuala Lumpur on flight OD-205, was intercepted at Terminal 3 based on profile-based targeting. An examination of her trolley bag led to the discovery of 30 polythene pouches containing suspected ganja (cannabis) weighing 15,015.5 grammes (net weight)," the department said.

items.title: Businessman sentenced to 30 years’ jail, 24 strokes for trafficking more than 77kg of meth
items.summary: IPOH, Sept 9 — A businessman was sentenced to 30 years in prison and 24 strokes of the cane by the High Court here today after being found guilty of two counts of trafficking more than 77 kilogrammes (kg) of methamphetamine five years ago. The court sentenced him to 30 years in prison and 12 strokes of the cane for the first and second counts respectively. According to the first charge, Liew is accused of distributing 74,477.8 grammes (74.48 kg) of methamphetamine, at the Gopeng Toll Plaza, towards the entrance to the highway before the toll payment counter, in the Kampar district at about 7.30 pm, June 23, 2021.

items.title: Eleven men, including college student, claim trial to armed rioting charge outside Air Itam school
items.summary: GEORGE TOWN, Sept 9 — Eleven men, including a college student, reportedly pleaded not guilty in the Magistrate’s Court here today to a charge of rioting while armed with objects that could be used as weapons. The accused were named as Mohamad Nun Mohamad Jupri, 34; V. Rathakisnan, 22; Soman Sri Mahen Deren, 19; Muhammad Haikal Mohammad Rafiq, 19; Chad Sebastian George Albert, 19; Elijah Yong, 19; Cheow Junnuo, 24; Tony Yen Chun Yun, 19; R. Divagar, 20; Muhammad Amirul Hafiz Abdullah, 21; and Ng Chern Yeow, 24. Police previously detained 23 people to assist in investigations into the armed riot.

items.title: Six civil servants, five agents remanded over alleged falsified documents for illegal vehicle ownership transfers
items.summary: IPOH, Sept 9 — Eleven individuals, including six civil servants and five agents, have been remanded for six days to assist investigations into the alleged submission of falsified documents to facilitate illegal vehicle ownership transfers involving 16 registration numbers. Magistrate Norizan Riduan allowed the remand application, which runs from today until Sept 14, at the Magistrate’s Court here today. “Initial investigations found that the alleged offence took place in 2025, with the agents suspected of conspiring with civil servants to submit falsified documents to enable vehicle ownership transfers to be carried out illegally,” the source said.

items.title: Four killed after car carrying three foreign nationals collides with lorry in Telupid
items.summary: KOTA KINABALU, Sept 9 — Four people were killed after the car they were travelling in collided with a lorry in Kampung Gambaron, Telupid, about 230 kilometres from here, this morning. The Sabah Fire and Rescue Department Operations Centre said it received an emergency call on the crash involving two vehicles travelling in opposite directions at 7.28 am. “Four victims were in the car and were extricated by firefighters, the Royal Malaysia Police (PDRM) and the Civil Defence Force before medical personnel from the Health Ministry (MOH) confirmed that they died at the scene,” it said in a statement today.

items.title: Guan Eng submits ‘Malaysia Agenda 12’ package to Anwar, proposes RM25b in interest-free MSME loans
items.summary: In a hand-delivered letter yesterday, the DAP adviser proposed RM25 billion in interest-free and collateral-free loans for 500,000 micro, small and medium enterprises (MSMEs), alongside a one-year interest moratorium on their existing bank loans. “The banking industry can afford to bear the cost of the interest moratorium on existing MSME loans for one year,” he said. Lim estimated that financing the interest-free loans would cost RM1 billion annually at a 4 per cent interest rate, citing the banking industry’s RM54.8 billion profit before tax in 2025 — a 13.5 per cent increase from 2024.

items.title: Another Malaysian pilot arrested over Jakarta drug syndicate probe, says Bukit Aman
items.summary: KUALA SELANGOR, Sept 9 — Another local pilot has been arrested to assist in investigations in connection with the detention of a Malaysion co-pilot in Jakarta in July for suspected involvement in an international drug trafficking syndicate. Bukit Aman Narcotics Crime Investigation Department (NCID) director Datuk Hussein Omar Khan said the Malaysian man, in his 30s, was arrested on Monday (Sept 7) in the Klang Valley. “Police seized various types of drugs, including 61.26kg of methylenedioxymethamphetamine (MDMA) liquid, ecstasy pills (0.79kg), cannabis flower (6.09kg), Erimin 5 pills (3.80kg), cannabis (11.13kg), methamphetamine (3.25kg), cannabis-laced biscuits (870 grammes), ketamine (490 grammes) and MDMA powder (480 grammes).

items.title: Sarawak govt to channel RM100,000 to each family of FDS helicopter crash victims
items.summary: KUCHING, Sept 9 — The Sarawak State Government will channel a contribution of RM100,000 to each family of personnel involved in the Flying Doctor Service (FDS) helicopter crash in Long Lellang, yesterday. In a statement on social media by the Sarawak Public Communications Unit (UKAS), the state government announced it will also fully cover the education fees of the victims’ children who are still in school through the Sarawak Foundation. “Sarawak Premier Tan Sri Abang Johari Tun Openg agreed that the assistance be channelled as a sign of the Sarawak State Government’s concern to help ease the burden of the families and the next of kin involved.

items.title: Hadi calls for abolition of ‘colonial laws’ to make Syariah rule supreme in Malaysia
items.summary: KUALA LUMPUR, Sept 9 — PAS president Tan Sri Abdul Hadi Awang has called for the abolition of laws he described as colonial legacies, alleging that these were obstacles to the unfettered implementation of Syariah law in Malaysia. In the statement, titled “Merdeka: Hapus Undang-Undang Penjajah Yang Sekat Pelaksanaan Islam” (”Independence: Abolish Colonial Laws That Obstruct the Implementation of Islam”), the Marang MP argued that true independence cannot be realised while laws inherited from British rule continue to limit Islam’s position above man-made legislation. “Colonial-legacy laws must be abolished to ensure the true meaning of independence can be fully realised,” Hadi said in the statement.

items.title: Negeri Sembilan royal dispute: Rembau Undang says MB sign-off cannot validate flawed proclamation
items.summary: SEREMBAN, Sept 9 — Rembau Undang Dato’ Sedia Raja Haji Hassan bin Haji Ab. Hamid today said the Menteri Besar’s signature could not validate a proclamation concerning the position of the Yang di-Pertuan Besar of Negeri Sembilan if the process leading to it was flawed. In a statement, Hassan said the main question was not whether the proclamation existed or how many people had signed it, but whether the process complied with the Negeri Sembilan Constitution and Adat Perpatih.
